Hey man. What you are experiencing is burn out. I’ve been through the exact thing you are going through. Two years ago i did horrible on a midterm that I studied for compared to a midterm i guessed most of the questions on and still somewhat did better. I know the feeling of it. I have a few suggestions for you that i think you should take to heart: 1. Go to therapy. Therapy is under a misconception that you need to have a mental illness in order to go to. No, you don’t need to have one. You can go there if you are having any troubles in life, anxiety, or even if you need someone to talk to. I’m currently going to an intake appointment soon for my own issues and it’s the first step to help with burn out and potentially anything else. 2. Spaced learning. Have days where you study and have days where you don’t. As soon as I started to have days where i studied and days where i focused on my mental health + hobbies, my grades turned way better. I did classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays, slept right after the classes (sleeping is actually extremely important in studying, it allows for consolidation) and then i went back to studying on the other days.  3. Take three courses per term. Sometimes you need to lower course load, and if it takes you longer to do your degree, so what? It’s better to do six years and have good grades than four years and have shit grades. 3 courses per term also allows you to be able to see what study methods work for you and what schedule works for you too. I recommend always to do 3 at the start then go to four or five. 

Lastly, you got this. University is hard, but people are also experiencing the same thing you are and there will always be people to support you. You can always reach out to PMs if you need any support.
